title: Water to store for the group at one gallon per person per day, the amount FEMA, CDC and the Red Cross give for drinking, cooking and basic hygiene; no source opened says it covers flushing toilets, bathing or laundry, so plan water for those separately.

drinkPerPersonDay.note: At least 1 gallon (3.8 L) per person per day: for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and other uses (CDC); for drinking and sanitation (Ready.gov); for drinking plus food preparation and hygiene (FEMA). Store more for children, nursing mothers, pregnant women, sick people, a medical emergency, pets, or a warm climate; no source gives an amount for these.

planDays.note: CDC: 3 days, and a 2-week supply if possible. Red Cross: a 2-week supply at home, 3 days to take when you evacuate. FEMA: at least a 2-week supply. NYS emergency services: be ready to manage on your own for at least 10 days. NYS Department of Health: 3 days. Ready.gov: several days. The planner uses 2 weeks.

lbPerGallon.note: A US gallon of water weighs 8.33 lb (USGS).

sources.name: Ready.gov (FEMA), Water
sources.used: 1 gallon per person per day for drinking and sanitation, for several days; a normally active person needs about three quarters of a gallon of fluid a day; children, nursing mothers, sick people, a medical emergency and warm climates may need more; in very hot temperatures water needs can double (the hot-weather extra)

sources.name: Ready.gov (FEMA), Emergency Supply List
sources.used: water item: one gallon per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation

sources.name: FEMA, American Red Cross and USDA, Food and Water in an Emergency
sources.used: store at least 1 gallon per person per day including food preparation and hygiene; at least a two-week supply; drinking need of at least two quarts a day, which hot environments can double; children, nursing mothers and ill people need more

sources.name: CDC, How to Create an Emergency Water Supply (reviewed June 27, 2025)
sources.used: at least 1 gallon per person per day for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and other uses; 3 days, and a 2-week supply if possible; store more for pregnant women, sick people, pets or a hot climate

sources.name: American Red Cross, Survival Kit Supplies
sources.used: one gallon per person per day; 3-day supply for evacuation, 2-week supply for home

sources.name: NYS Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services, Before an Emergency Happens
sources.used: one gallon per person per day; be prepared to make it on your own for at least 10 days (its kit list says supplies to last up to 10 days); plan for pets' water

sources.name: NYS Department of Health, family emergency preparedness leaflet (publication 7009, 11/14)
sources.used: at least one gallon per person per day for three days, for drinking and household use

sources.name: USGS Water Science School, Facts About Water
sources.used: a gallon of water weighs 8.33 pounds; 1 gallon is 3.7854 liters

sources.name: NIST Special Publication 811, Guide for the Use of the International System of Units, 1995 edition, Appendix B.8 (withdrawn 2018; the value agrees with USGS)
